source: NCDPI, NC Math 1 Standard Course of Study (https://www.dpi.nc.gov/media/4012/open). Descriptions paraphrased.

standards.NC.M1.N-RN.2: Rewrite expressions with integer exponents using the properties of exponents.
standards.NC.M1.A-SSE.1a: Identify and interpret parts of linear, exponential and quadratic expressions (terms, factors, coefficients).
standards.NC.M1.A-SSE.1b: Interpret expressions made of several parts as a combination of meaningful pieces.
standards.NC.M1.A-SSE.3: Factor quadratic expressions to reveal the solutions of an equation or zeros of a function.
standards.NC.M1.A-APR.1: Add and subtract quadratic expressions; add, subtract and multiply linear expressions.
standards.NC.M1.A-APR.3: Understand the relationship between factors of a quadratic, solutions of the equation and zeros of the function.
standards.NC.M1.A-CED.1: Create equations and inequalities in one variable (linear, exponential, quadratic) and use them to solve problems.
standards.NC.M1.A-CED.2: Create and graph equations in two variables for linear, exponential and quadratic relationships.
standards.NC.M1.A-CED.3: Create systems of linear equations and inequalities to model situations in context.
standards.NC.M1.A-CED.4: Solve formulas for a quantity of interest using the same reasoning as solving equations.
standards.NC.M1.A-REI.1: Justify each step in solving linear and quadratic equations.
standards.NC.M1.A-REI.3: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable.
standards.NC.M1.A-REI.4: Solve quadratic equations by taking square roots and by factoring.
standards.NC.M1.A-REI.5: Explain why replacing one equation in a system by a sum with a multiple of the other keeps the same solutions.
standards.NC.M1.A-REI.6: Use tables, graphs or algebra to solve systems of linear equations and interpret the solution in context.
standards.NC.M1.A-REI.10: Understand that the graph of a two-variable equation is the set of all its solutions.
standards.NC.M1.A-REI.11: Explain why the x-coordinates of intersection points solve f(x) = g(x).
standards.NC.M1.A-REI.12: Represent the solutions of a linear inequality or system of linear inequalities graphically as a region of the plane.
standards.NC.M1.F-IF.1: Understand that a function assigns exactly one output to each input; use function notation.
standards.NC.M1.F-IF.2: Use function notation to evaluate functions and interpret statements in context.
standards.NC.M1.F-IF.3: Recognize that recursively and explicitly defined sequences are functions whose domain is a subset of the integers.
standards.NC.M1.F-IF.4: Interpret key features (intercepts, intervals of increase/decrease, max/min) of functions in context.
standards.NC.M1.F-IF.5: Interpret a function's domain and range in context.
standards.NC.M1.F-IF.6: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change over a given interval.
standards.NC.M1.F-IF.7: Analyze linear, exponential and quadratic functions using different representations.
standards.NC.M1.F-IF.8a: Rewrite a quadratic function to reveal and explain its key features.
standards.NC.M1.F-IF.8b: Interpret the growth or decay rate of an exponential function.
standards.NC.M1.F-IF.9: Compare key features of two functions given in different representations.
standards.NC.M1.F-BF.1a: Build linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, from a graph, description or input-output pairs.
standards.NC.M1.F-BF.1b: Build a new function by adding, subtracting or multiplying functions.
standards.NC.M1.F-BF.2: Translate between explicit and recursive forms of arithmetic and geometric sequences and use them to model situations.
standards.NC.M1.F-LE.1: Identify linear vs exponential situations by equal differences vs equal factors over equal intervals.
standards.NC.M1.F-LE.3: Compare linear, exponential and quadratic growth; exponential growth eventually exceeds the others.
standards.NC.M1.F-LE.5: Interpret the parameters of linear and exponential functions in context.
standards.NC.M1.G-GPE.4: Use coordinates to solve problems about polygons (perimeter, area, classification).
standards.NC.M1.G-GPE.5: Use slopes to identify parallel and perpendicular lines and write their equations.
standards.NC.M1.G-GPE.6: Use coordinates to find the midpoint or a point that partitions a segment in a given ratio.
standards.NC.M1.S-ID.1: Use technology to represent single-variable data with histograms and box plots.
standards.NC.M1.S-ID.2: Compare center and spread of two or more data sets.
standards.NC.M1.S-ID.3: Examine the effect of outliers on shape, center and spread.
standards.NC.M1.S-ID.6a: Fit a least-squares regression line to linear data with technology and use it to solve problems.
standards.NC.M1.S-ID.6b: Assess the fit of a linear function by analyzing residuals.
standards.NC.M1.S-ID.6c: Fit an exponential function to data with technology.
standards.NC.M1.S-ID.7: Interpret the slope and intercept of a linear model in context.
standards.NC.M1.S-ID.8: Analyze patterns and describe relationships between two variables using the correlation coefficient.
